detail.body:
## Motivation

A streaming request that the scheduler rejects before producing any output (e.g. `The request queue is full.` when `--max-queued-requests` is reached) is answered with **HTTP 200** and an in-band `data: {"error": ...}` event, while the same rejection on a non-streaming request is a **503**. Clients and proxies that retry on 429/503 never see the status. We hit this on a production batch endpoint during a load surge: a large share of streaming replies were 200s that carried no content.

This is an alternative to #28175, which targets the same problem. Reviewing #28175 found that:
- `/v1/messages` (Anthropic) iterates `_generate_chat_stream` directly, so the new exception landed in its generic handler. A queue-full rejection became `api_error "Internal server error"` (still HTTP 200), and a stack trace was logged per rejected request.
- The gRPC bridge's streaming RPC drops `status_code`, so the error became a normal final chunk.
- The `isinstance(status_code, HTTPStatus)` gate never matches under msgpack IPC, where `status_code` decodes to a plain `int`.
- It adds a second abort-to-HTTP mapping (a new exception class) next to the one `TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason` already has, and the two produce different `error.type` values.

## Modifications

- **Chat and completions generators.** When an error abort arrives before the first chunk, they now raise the same exceptions `TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason` raises for a non-stream abort: `ValueError` for 400, `HTTPException` for 500/503. The streaming handlers already wait for the first chunk before sending the status line, and `handle_request` already maps these exceptions, so stream and non-stream get the same status and body. No new exception class or `except` arm is needed.
- **One shared set of statuses.** `HTTP_ERROR_ABORT_STATUSES` (in `io_struct`) lists the abort statuses that are answered as an HTTP error, and both `TokenizerManager` and the stream path use it. Other statuses (e.g. an EPD 504), and any abort after the first chunk, keep the in-band error event.
- **msgpack IPC.** `error_abort_status` also accepts a plain `int` `status_code`. Before, such aborts streamed with no error at all.
- **`/v1/messages`.** It pulls the first OpenAI chunk before committing HTTP 200, so a rejection is a real `503 overloaded_error` or `400 invalid_request_error`. The pre-first-chunk `ValueError` branch inside `_generate_anthropic_stream` could no longer be reached, so it is removed.
- **gRPC bridge.** For a `stream: true` request, an error response is delivered as an in-band `{"error": ...}` chunk, which the streaming RPC can carry, instead of a bare error body in the final chunk. `stream: false` requests on the same RPC are unchanged.

**Behavior change.** For `stream: true`, a pre-first-chunk rejection is now `application/json` with a non-200 status, instead of `text/event-stream` with an error event under HTTP 200. That is the intent, but consumers that parsed the SSE error event for this case (routers, gateways) will now see the HTTP status instead. `/v1/messages` streams now send response headers only once the first token is ready, as the OpenAI routes already do.

**Not covered (follow-ups):**
- Native `/generate` streaming, Ollama and the Responses API still answer a pre-first-chunk rejection with 200.
- Non-streaming `/v1/messages` still maps a 503 abort to `500 api_error`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. No change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

Run on a Linux CPU VM installed the way CI installs it:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py` | 154 passed |
| `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_completions.py` | 22 passed |
| `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py` | 65 passed |
| `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_grpc_bridge.py` | 7 passed |
| `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py` | 39 passed |

New tests:
- Pre-first-chunk 503, 400 and plain-int 503 through `handle_request` (chat and completions).
- A 504 that still streams in-band.
- The `/v1/messages` 503/400 rejection, a pre-first-chunk `ValueError` that becomes a 400, and the first chunk being kept.
- gRPC streaming in-band error, no re-wrapping of an existing envelope, and `stream: false` keeping its status code.

The existing mid-stream abort tests now stream one normal chunk first, so they keep covering the in-band path.

Mutation-checked. Each of the 12 guards below was removed or inverted in turn, and each mutant made a targeted test fail:
- the pre-stream raise, in chat and in completions;
- raising even after the first chunk;
- `int` normalization;
- the status-set restriction;
- the 400 → `ValueError` mapping;
- the Anthropic kick-start;
- the Anthropic 503 message;
- the gRPC in-band branch, its `stream` flag check, and the envelope unwrap.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+def error_abort_status(finish_reason: Optional[dict]) -> Optional[HTTPStatus]:
+    """Return the HTTP status of an abort that carries an error ``status_code``.
+
+    Returns None for any other finish, including a graceful abort without a
+    status code (e.g. ``/abort_request``), which streams as a normal finish.
+    ``status_code`` is an ``HTTPStatus`` under pickle IPC and a plain ``int``
+    under msgpack IPC, so both are accepted.
+    """
+    if not finish_reason or finish_reason.get("type") != "abort":
+        return None
+    code = finish_reason.get("status_code")
+    if code is None:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return HTTPStatus(int(code))
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return None
+
+
+def raise_pre_stream_abort(status: HTTPStatus, message: str) -> None:
+    """Raise an error abort that arrived before a stream yielded its first chunk.
+
+    Streaming handlers wait for the generator's first chunk before sending the
+    response status line. Raising here instead of yielding an in-band error
+    chunk lets an admission-time rejection (e.g. "The request queue is full.")
+    reach the client as a real HTTP error rather than an error event under
+    HTTP 200. It raises exactly when, and what,
+    ``TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason`` raises for a non-stream
+    abort, so ``handle_request`` answers both modes with the same status and
+    body. For any other status it returns, and the caller streams the error
+    in-band.
+    """
+    if status not in HTTP_ERROR_ABORT_STATUSES:
+        return
+    if status == HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+    raise HTTPException(status_code=status.value, detail=message)
+

+class _KwargsRecordingCallback:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def __call__(self, payload, **kwargs):
+        self.calls.append((payload, kwargs))
+        return _ChunkStatus.Ready
+

+class _ErrorResponseServing:
+    """OpenAI serving whose handle_request rejects the request, as it does for
+    a stream aborted before its first chunk (e.g. queue full)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, enveloped=False):
+        self.enveloped = enveloped
+
+    async def handle_request(self, request, raw_request):
+        error = ErrorResponse(
+            object="error",
+            message="The request queue is full.",
+            type="503",
+            code=503,
+        ).model_dump()
+        if self.enveloped:
+            error = {"error": error}
+        return ORJSONResponse(content=error, status_code=503)
+
+
+def _make_openai_runtime_handle(enveloped=False):
+    handle = RuntimeHandle.__new__(RuntimeHandle)
+    handle._openai_serving_classes = {"chat": _ErrorResponseServing(enveloped)}
+    handle._get_openai_request_class = lambda serving_key: (
+        lambda **fields: SimpleNamespace(**fields)
+    )
+    return handle
+

+class TestOpenAIGrpcErrorResponses(CustomTestCase):

+        asyncio.run(
+            handle._run_openai_request(
+                "chat",
+                json.dumps({"stream": stream}).encode("utf-8"),
+                callback,
+                # submit_openai_chat always runs the streaming RPC; the
+                # request body's "stream" flag picks the response shape.
+                streaming=True,
